profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting at a university-affiliated research software institute that supports long-lived cyberinfrastructure tools for science collaborations. The institute has just synthesized initial findings from interviews with leaders of exemplar cyberinfrastructure software projects about what makes software sustainable over time, and leadership wants those findings packaged for an upcoming steering committee review. At the same time, the community-engagement side hopes the same work can seed a later public-facing resource for principal investigators and project leads. The agenda is to decide what the first deliverable will be, how the interview-backed examples will be incorporated, what engineering work is actually needed, who owns each piece, and what being 'ready by next Friday' entails. The expected outcome is a concrete plan for a first-cut sustainability recommendations package, with assigned responsibilities and a timeline that appears mutually agreed.

members.name: Priya Natarajan
members.expertise: Platform engineering, release coordination, documentation pipelines, research software operations
members.background: Priya leads the engineering group that maintains the institute's website, publication pipeline, and internal dissemination tooling; she previously handled release engineering for an academic HPC middleware project where last-minute scope expansion routinely disrupted delivery.
members.private_state: Priya wants a plan that can be executed with almost no new platform work because her team is in the middle of an infrastructure migration, and she is wary of anything framed in the meeting that could quietly turn an internal briefing artifact into a product commitment.
hidden_assumptions: A 'first cut' for findings work means a polished but essentially static artifact that is good enough for internal review and can later be expanded if needed.

When people say 'the project examples from the study,' they usually mean the already publication-safe interview summaries and approved excerpts the comms team has cleaned up, not every raw interview case discussed in the research process.

If engineering agrees to 'wire up the examples,' the obvious low-risk path is to place selected excerpts into the existing static site templates and front-matter files rather than introduce a reusable structured content layer.
'Ready by next Friday' means leadership can review a stable draft in the steering committee materials, even if it is not yet suitable to circulate outside the institute.
Because this meeting is about planning a packaging effort, any broader externalization assumptions would be surfaced explicitly if they were intended.

members.name: Ethan Morales
members.expertise: Developer relations, product strategy, stakeholder communication, research community engagement
members.background: Ethan works with PIs, user communities, and partner institutions to turn internal research outputs into outward-facing resources that can support adoption and future funding; he previously led outreach for an NSF-funded open-source data platform where lightweight MVPs often became durable public assets.
members.private_state: Ethan wants this deliverable to be intentionally reusable from the start so it can support external conversations with project leads and funders soon after the steering committee review, and he worries that a purely presentational artifact will create rework and lose momentum.
hidden_assumptions: A 'first cut' means a minimal but real productized version of the findings—small in scope, but already shaped for reuse beyond the immediate review meeting.

When people refer to 'the project examples from the study,' they mean the set of exemplar cases the study is drawing its authority from as a whole, not just the subset already cleaned for publication.

If the team says they will 'wire up the examples,' the sensible interpretation is to capture them in some lightweight structured form now so they can later support tags, filters, or repackaging without manual re-entry.
'Ready by next Friday' means something concrete enough to show in partner-facing prep conversations—a stable link, reviewed copy, and no caveats that it is still for internal eyes only.

Because leadership asked for findings that can inform broader community guidance, everyone already sees this deliverable as the beginning of an outward-facing resource unless someone states otherwise.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to produce a 'first cut' of the sustainability findings package.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 hears 'first cut' as a presentable internal artifact: a static recommendations page and companion PDF that are polished enough for steering committee review but not designed as a reusable product.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 hears 'first cut' as an MVP: modest and incomplete, but already intentionally shaped as a reusable, externally legible resource.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both participants regularly use 'first cut' to signal an early version, and the phrase sounds naturally aligned because the disagreement is not about whether the artifact is preliminary, but about what kind of preliminary artifact is implied.

misalignment_points.topic: Which examples count as the study examples
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss including 'the project examples from the study' under each recommendation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the publication-safe subset of interview cases that already have cleaned summaries and approved quotations ready to slot into a deliverable.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the study's exemplar project set in the broader sense—the full body of cases the recommendations are meant to be grounded in, whether or not every summary has already been publication-prepped.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are referring to legitimate examples connected to the same study, and neither needs to state a count for the phrase to feel complete; the divergence hides inside an unspoken narrowing from 'the study' to 'the already usable study materials.'

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree engineering will 'wire up the examples' so each recommendation has supporting cases.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means manually embedding selected excerpts and links into the existing static site and PDF workflow using current templates and content files.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means introducing a lightweight structured representation of the examples now—such as tagged YAML, a sheet export, or another simple content layer—so the same examples can be reorganized and reused later.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both execution paths can honestly be described as 'wiring up the examples,' and the difference concerns invisible implementation affordances rather than the visible recommendation content discussed in the meeting, so it does not naturally trigger clarification.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on having the package 'ready by next Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 takes 'ready' to mean internally reviewable and stable: leadership can open the draft in the steering committee folder, read coherent copy, and leave comments before anything public happens.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 takes 'ready' to mean shareable without qualification: a stable link, finished enough visuals and copy, and no internal-only framing that would prevent him from using it in partner-facing discussion.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Deadline language in planning meetings often bundles timing and completion state into one shorthand phrase, and because both participants are trying to move quickly, each assumes the other's normal threshold for 'ready' matches their own workflow context.

turns.inner_thought: I need to keep this tightly bounded. My team is already deep in the infrastructure migration, and I do not want a planning meeting about packaging findings to turn into an implicit product commitment. A first cut should be a polished internal artifact for the steering committee packet, and ready by next Friday should mean a stable draft leadership can review, not something we have to treat like a public launch.
turns.utterance: Thanks for jumping on. We need a concrete plan to turn the sustainability interview findings into a first cut for the steering committee, and we need it ready by next Friday. I'd like to leave with clear ownership on the content, the examples, and whatever engineering support is actually needed.

turns.inner_thought: Good. If we anchor on a first cut, we can keep scope modest but still make something real enough to reuse right away. I want this framed as practical guidance that can carry past the review meeting. And when I say the project examples from the study, I'm thinking of the exemplar case set broadly, not just the already publication-prepped subset.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. I think the package should read as practical recommendations, with the project examples from the study under each one, so it works for the review meeting and still has some life after that.

turns.inner_thought: Fastest path is existing templates, existing front matter, existing PDF export. No new schema, no content layer, no tooling detour. If engineering wires up the examples, we'll manually place selected approved excerpts into the current static workflow under each recommendation.

turns.utterance: That works, as long as the examples still give a representative sense of how the projects support each recommendation.

turns.inner_thought: I'll add lightweight labels now so the content is easier to reorganize later by theme or audience. That should fit naturally with wiring up the examples and help this first cut function as the seed of something reusable. I don't need to get into downstream use cases explicitly.
turns.utterance: Works for me. I'll also add a lightweight labeling pass for themes and likely use cases so the first cut is easier to reuse once it's out.

turns.utterance: That's fine—if you include that in the draft copy by Wednesday, engineering can fold it in and have something ready by Friday.

turns.inner_thought: Perfect. Ready by Friday should mean I have a stable, legible link I can start using to prep next steps with partners and leadership. I'll keep it phrased broadly so we're not reopening scope here.
